code.text: Dental encounter summary — to pediatric endocrinologist

assessor.display: Dr. David Watson, DDS — Cornell Scott-Hill Health Center

summary: Timothy Jones, six-year-old male with Type 1 diabetes (E10.9), seen 2026-05-28 for dental evaluation. Aggressive periodontitis (K05.211), localized, slight, confirmed. Periodontal disease progression accelerated by poorly controlled glycemia - this relationship is bidirectional: periodontitis also exacerbates glycemic dysregulation and may complicate insulin management. Scaling and root planing performed (D4341 x2). Chlorhexidine 2.5% chip placed at affected periodontal sites (D4381). Most recent HbA1c requested from chart if available - not available in records received. Recommend glycemic review given periodontal disease burden in the context of ongoing diabetes management.

note.text: Structured summary to the pediatric endocrinologist (Yale Children's Diabetes Program) via Connie — the second of the two simultaneous Interaction 4 summaries. Its clinical point is the bidirectional oral-systemic relationship: it carries the NEW periodontal->glycemic risk Flag (flag-perio-glycemic-risk), which points in the OPPOSITE direction from the Interaction 1 diabetes->periodontal Flag. The two Flags must not be conflated.
